newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine may lower key rate in January - central bank.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine may lower key rate in January - central bank.

text.p: Ukraine's central bank may lower its refinancing rate in January to reflect the country's steadily slowing rate of inflation, the bank's chairman said at the weekend.
"The refinancing rate may be lowered in January, since a slowdown in inflation has given us the ability to do this," Viktor Yushchenko told a news conference on Saturday.
He did not say what size the reduction could be.
The refinancing rate at which commercial banks borrow funds from the central bank is currently 40 percent and was 105 percent at the beginning of 1996.
Yushchenko said annual inflation likely would be 40.5 percent this year, after 181.7 percent in 1995.
But he said that the decision to lower the refinancing rate would require political support from Ukraine's Finance Ministry.
